note: Verifies cosign v3.1.1 signing BEHAVIOR and Sigstore bundle SHAPE, not timing. No statistical distribution applies: each observation is a deterministic pass/fail from running the documented command sequence. Source of the central artifact: bundle-default-redacted.json.

bundle_shape_matrix.subject: cosign v3.1.1 (windows/amd64), sign-blob with a local keypair
bundle_shape_matrix.method: Generate keypair, sign a blob two ways, inspect verificationMaterial keys of each --bundle output.

offline_signing.command: cosign signing-config create --no-default-rekor --no-default-tsa --no-default-fulcio --no-default-oidc --out signing-config-offline.json  &&  cosign sign-blob --key cosign.key --signing-config signing-config-offline.json --bundle artifact-offline.sigstore.json artifact.txt

behaviors_verified.claim: A key-based `sign-blob` (no Fulcio/keyless involved) STILL uploads to the public transparency log by default: the bundle's verificationMaterial contains a tlogEntries entry on rekor.sigstore.dev (hashedrekord v0.0.1, with inclusionProof + inclusionPromise) AND an RFC3161 TSA timestamp. 'Signed with a key' does not mean 'offline'.

`--tlog-upload=false` is deprecated in v3 and is rejected when combined with a signing-config. cosign prints: 'Flag --tlog-upload has been deprecated, prefer using a --signing-config file with no transparency log services', and errors 'Error: --tlog-upload=false is not supported with --signing-config or --use-signing-config.' The offline path is now a `--signing-config` file created with --no-default-rekor/--no-default-tsa.
behaviors_verified.evidence: run.sh step 3; command stderr recorded in firsthand notes

behaviors_verified.claim: Signing with the offline signing-config produces the SAME bundle.v0.3+json mediaType but its verificationMaterial has only ['publicKey'] — zero tlogEntries, no timestamp. Same format, two shapes: 'public-log' vs 'self-contained'.
behaviors_verified.evidence: run.sh step 3 diff of the two bundles' verificationMaterial keys

behaviors_verified.claim: For OCI image signatures, `cosign triangulate` warns it is deprecated and 'will be removed in v4.0.0 — use `oras discover` or `cosign tree`'. Signatures attach both as the legacy `sha256-<digest>.sig` tag AND as an OCI referrer — the tag-based discovery -> referrers-API transition that v3->v4 is steering toward.
behaviors_verified.evidence: run.sh step 4 (optional, needs local Docker registry); command stderr recorded in firsthand notes

behaviors_verified.claim: Verifying an offline (no-tlog) signature requires `--insecure-ignore-tlog=true`, and cosign prints 'Skipping tlog verification is an insecure practice...'. The tool itself flags that dropping transparency is a real auditability trade-off, not a free win.
behaviors_verified.evidence: run.sh step 4 verify; command stderr recorded in firsthand notes

not_measured.linux_macos: Only windows/amd64 was run. cosign is cross-platform Go; behavior is expected to match but was not measured on other OSes.
not_measured.keyless_fulcio_flow: This run covers key-based signing only. The keyless (Fulcio OIDC) flow is discussed in the post conceptually, not measured here.
not_measured.rekor_v2_internals: Rekor v2 tile/tessera storage internals are cited from Sigstore docs, not inspected firsthand.

cited_not_measured.claim: Sigstore bundle spec v0.3 / signing-config v0.2 media types.
Latest cosign is v3.1.2 (2026-07-17); v4 will remove the deprecated flags.
